title: Money on the road and raising four daughters
summary: About $10 a night with little tax; theater scale was $73.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: How as the money on the road?
Well, couldn't say it was much. We didn't make but about $10.00 a night.

It was in the thirties. But that was during the Depression. You didn't have unions -- didn't have all that union tax to pay. Only tax we had to pay was like the -- the scales in the town we were playing in might be 50 cents or 60 cents.

That was all. You didn't have income tax, you didn't have nothing. That was all clear money. And that was enough money for me to send money home and still have money to live on. I don't know how the heck we'd do it. That was a heck of a ...
Sure, I was raising these four girls.
Now you sit and you wonder, how could I do it. Like theaters only played $73.00. That was the scale.
Where were you living in Chicago?
Oh, on the Southside, between 59th and Michigan. I lived there for a long time. 58th and Michigan.
